stories.headline: Zelenskyi offers Finland drone technology cooperation and defense partnership
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyi proposed a drone deal to Finnish PM Petteri Orpo during their meeting in Armenia at the European Political Community summit on May 3. Orpo confirmed Zelenskyi offered cooperation on drone technology, combat expertise, and military partnership, which Orpo termed 'interesting.' The proposal follows recent drone incidents over Finnish airspace.

stories.headline: Political discourse deterioration raises concerns as election nears; opposition launches interpellation against Orpo government
stories.summary: Prime Minister Orpo expressed concern about deteriorating political discussion culture in Finland, citing the heated A-studio debate between Sofia Virta (Greens) and Wille Rydman (Finns Party) on April 29. Opposition parties (SDP, Greens, Left Alliance, Centre Party) filed an interpellation on May 1 seeking to bring down the Orpo government, citing economic policy failures and broken election promises.

stories.headline: Finance Minister Purra faces controversy over electoral promises regarding cuts to low-income benefits
stories.summary: Valtiovarainminister Riikka Purra (Finns Party) faced scrutiny over whether the Finns Party broke its 2023 election promises not to cut benefits for the poorest. Yle Ykkösaamu show highlighted discrepancies between Purra's pre-election statements and current government policy. Multiple opposition figures, including Eveliina Heinäluoma (SDP), demanded explanations.

stories.headline: President Stubb participates in international diplomatic events and reflects on Russia policy
stories.summary: President Alexander Stubb attended King Charles XVI Gustaf's 80th birthday celebration in Sweden on April 30 with his spouse Suzanne Innes-Stubb. Stubb also received an Estonian state visit from President Alar Karis, visited Prague for Czech-Finnish bilateral relations, and gave interviews reflecting on historical Finland-Russia relations, stating Finland was 'too soft' on Russia post-Georgia.

stories.headline: Defense Minister Häkkänen announces Finland joining international drone coalition before summer
stories.summary: Defense Minister Antti Häkkänen (National Coalition) announced that Finland will join the international drone coalition supporting Ukraine before summer 2026. The coalition aims to provide drones to the front lines and allows Finland to strengthen domestic drone industry partnerships and increase military support to Ukraine.

stories.headline: Defense Minister Häkkänen seeks constitutional amendment for security screening of foreign property acquisitions
stories.summary: Defense Minister Antti Häkkänen (National Coalition) is pushing for a constitutional law amendment to allow retrospective scrutiny of property purchases made by individuals acting for Russia, citing national security concerns. The issue follows the failed Fennovoima-Rosatom nuclear power project in Pyhäjoki. Häkkänen also faced criticism over the timing and process of nuclear energy legislation changes.

stories.headline: Suomi.fi portal abuse in online scams; police warn of increasing fraud attempts
stories.summary: Finnish police reported a sharp increase in online fraud schemes exploiting the newly updated Suomi.fi government portal. Scammers impersonate government agencies and financial institutions to trick citizens into transferring money to fake 'security accounts.' March saw 172 network fraud cases involving Suomi.fi impersonation in Eastern Finland alone. Police advise citizens on how to identify legitimate vs. fraudulent messages.

stories.headline: Bank of Finland ceases crowdfunding data collection; domestic investment activity remains strong
stories.summary: The Bank of Finland announced it is ending data collection on crowdfunding activity, as registered crowdfunding intermediaries' operations have contracted to marginal levels. Household investment in Finnish equities and investment funds remains robust, with Finnish households holding €52.4 billion in listed shares and €39.5 billion in domestic investment funds. Central bank monitors interest rate environment and housing loan trends.

stories.headline: OP payment system disruptions cause delays in salary and benefits processing
stories.summary: Osuuspankki (OP) experienced payment processing disruptions on Thursday morning, causing delays in salary and benefit transfers to customer accounts. Multiple banks reported receiving delayed payments, affecting customers across Finland. OP confirmed the technical issue was resolved during the morning, and payments began clearing by late morning.

stories.headline: 2027 parliamentary election campaign launches; parties announce first wave of candidates
stories.summary: Finnish political parties began announcing their first slate of candidates for the 2027 parliamentary elections. National Coalition (Kokoomus) named 13 candidates from Helsinki including entertainment personality Jone Nikula, Centre Party named candidates from Varsinais-Suomi, and Christian Democrats from Etelä-Savo. Election is scheduled for spring 2027, approximately one year away.

stories.headline: NATO strategic position reassessed amid US uncertainty and European defense initiatives
stories.summary: NATO is considering ending annual summit meetings to avoid potential confrontation with President Trump in his final year. European nations are bolstering independent defense capabilities, with the UK proposing a joint maritime force ('Northern Navies') with 9 European allies as a NATO complement. Poland's PM Donald Tusk warned NATO risks 'disintegration' due to US troop withdrawal announcements. NATO faces ammunition shortages and capability gaps exposed by Middle East tensions.
